why: TCP transport-layer services (multiplexing/demultiplexing, error checking). TCP internals are general data communications; the only networking leaf in the 2026 syllabus is TECH2 Unit 2's web architecture/HTTP/DNS leaf, which this does not touch.
SMTP client/server roles in mail relay. Email protocols are not in the 2026 syllabus; the TECH2 Unit 2 leaf covers web client-server communication over HTTP/HTTPS and DNS, not SMTP.
Network topology (physical vs logical arrangement) — explicitly a data communications topic with no leaf in either 2026 paper.
Time-division multiplexing frame/slot structure. Multiplexing belongs to data communications, which the 2026 syllabus dropped entirely.
Comparison of FDM/TDM/WDM multiplexing techniques — data communications, no corresponding leaf in TECH1 or TECH2.
UTP cabling and its use in DSL — transmission media, a data communications topic absent from the 2026 syllabus.
Properties of radio channels as a transmission medium — wireless data communications, not covered by any 2026 leaf.
Physics of optical fibre (total internal reflection) — transmission media, outside both 2026 papers.
Guided vs unguided transmission media — data communications, no leaf in the 2026 syllabus.
Network Management Systems and hardware/connection maps — network administration, not web architecture or hosting; nothing in TECH1 or TECH2 covers it.
Professional ethics/misuse from the software engineering code of conduct. The syllabus's only 'ethics and law' wording sits inside the AI-assisted web development leaf, which this does not test.
Definition of software (programs + documentation + configuration data) — software engineering fundamentals, dropped from the 2026 syllabus.
RAD as an SDLC process model acronym — software engineering process models, not covered by TECH1 or TECH2.
Choosing an SDLC process model based on user involvement — software engineering process models, off-syllabus.
Classification of evolutionary process models (spiral, incremental, concurrent) — software engineering, no 2026 leaf.
Fundamental activities of the software process (specification, design, validation, evolution) — software engineering, off-syllabus.
First step of the SDLC — systems analysis and software engineering lifecycle, absent from the 2026 syllabus.
Deliverable of the analysis phase (program specification) — systems analysis and design, which the 2026 syllabus does not contain.
White-box testing as structural testing — software testing, part of the dropped software engineering subject.
Alpha testing venue — software testing, off-syllabus.
Beta testing (real data in a real environment) — software testing, off-syllabus.

Conflicts handled by software configuration management (simultaneous updates, shared code, versions). Arguably adjacent to the 'Git version control' leaf in TECH2 Unit 2, but it tests an SE-textbook SCM list rather than any Git/CI-CD practice.
The four SCM tasks (identification, version control, auditing, status accounting) — software configuration management theory from software engineering, not the Git/CI-CD tooling leaf.
